questions.prompt: Why does Script Block Logging (Event ID 4104) matter more than Module Logging (4103) for reading obfuscated PowerShell?
options: 4104 events are stored for longer than 4103 events
4104 captures the full script text after PowerShell's own parser has evaluated it, which unwinds most obfuscation automatically
4103 is disabled by default on all Windows versions
questions.explanation: Script Block Logging records the script after PowerShell's parser has fully reconstructed it -- meaning Base64 encoding and most string-based obfuscation are already unwound by the time the event is written.

questions.prompt: What makes PSReadLine's ConsoleHost_history.txt different from the other logging sources in this lesson?
options: It requires Script Block Logging to be enabled first
It's a plain text file that requires no logging policy at all to exist, and records every interactively-typed command
It is automatically deleted after each session
questions.explanation: PSReadLine writes interactive command history to a plain text file by default, independent of any Group Policy logging setting -- making it valuable even in an environment where nothing else was turned on.

questions.prompt: Why can't missing Script Block Logging be fixed retroactively during an incident?
options: It can be fixed retroactively with the right tool
The logging only captures events going forward from when the policy takes effect, so activity before that point was never recorded
Retroactive logging requires a Microsoft support ticket
Only Domain Admins can enable it
questions.explanation: Logging policies only affect activity from the point they're applied onward -- there's no way to generate log entries for PowerShell activity that already happened before the setting was turned on.

questions.prompt: An analyst finds a 4103 module-logging event but no corresponding 4104 script-block event for the same activity window. What does this suggest?
options: This is completely normal and expected behavior
Logging is present at one layer but effectively blind at another during that same window -- worth investigating on its own
The host has no PowerShell installed
The 4103 event must be a false positive
questions.explanation: A gap between what module logging and script block logging each captured for the same window is itself a red flag worth investigating, not just an artifact of normal variation.
